coordinates: pixels in the full scan above, origin top left
method: Same conventions as bird-pigeon-pl755.json. Each lateral frame cropped from the full scan at 1.5x with a 25 px grid and raised contrast; points picked by eye, drawn back onto the crops (body line head->tail, wing line shoulder->tip) and corrected until they sat on the feature. head = eye; shoulder = where the near wing's leading edge leaves the body; wingTip = most distal primary of the near wing; tailTip = point of the (spread) tail fan farthest from the head. Angles use image coordinates with y up. bodyPitchDeg: angle of the tail->head line above the horizontal (nose up positive). wingElevationDeg: angle of shoulder->wingTip from the body's rearward axis (head->tail), positive toward the back (dorsal): 0 = wing lying back along the body, +90 = straight up from the back, beyond +/-90 = pointing forward, -90 = straight down. Side-view (projected) angles; projected length is recorded too. Stroke top/bottom = frames where the near wing tip is highest/lowest relative to the tail tip (image y). Wingbeat period from the frame lag between tops and between repeating silhouettes, times the catalogue interval. Bob: eye height corrected per frame by the y of the thick horizontal backdrop line (found with a darkness profile in a bird-free strip of each frame; 1541-1549 px, i.e. cameras aligned within +/-4 px), then a quadratic climb trend removed. Pigeon faces left.
frameBoxesNote: Listed in time order (frame 1 first), approximate to about 10 px; frame 1 is the rightmost (frames numbered 12 to 1 left to right).

timing.cyclesSource: muybridge-1887-catalogue (fraction of a cycle shown on the plate)
timing.observedComputed: tops of the stroke at frames 1, 7 and 12 (6 then 5 frames apart), i.e. 2 beats in 11 intervals = 5.5 frames x 21 ms = 116 ms; frames 3-12 also repeat at a lag of 5 (3~8, 4~9, 5~10, 6~11, 7~12) while 1-2 match 7-8 at a lag of 6, so the period is 5-6 frames: 7.9-9.5 Hz. Here the catalogue fraction agrees with the plate (unlike plates 755, 765).

frames.phase: top of stroke: wing near vertical over the back, tilted slightly forward of perpendicular to the body
frames.notes: Spread tail seen obliquely; tail tip = far edge of the fan.

frames.phase: mid-downstroke: wings spread sideways; the near wing projects below the body (lit underside), the far wing above it
frames.notes: Near wing taken as the lower one (camera slightly below the bird, so a laterally spread wing nearest the camera projects downward). Its tip is blurred. The far wing tip (about [3830,1423]) is recorded but not used.

frames.phase: bottom of stroke: near wing below and ahead of the shoulder, far wing ahead of the head at body level
frames.notes: Head is the dark blob at the base of the far wing; read with moderate confidence.

frames.phase: early upstroke: both wings swept forward at body level, blurred
frames.notes: Head hidden behind the forward-swept wings, so no body axis and no angles. Not measured.

frames.phase: upstroke: wing raised, partly flexed, dark upper surface
late upstroke: wing extended up and back in an arc, tip behind the shoulder
top of stroke: wing near vertical, tilted slightly forward
bottom of stroke: near wing below and ahead (lit underside), far wing up and ahead
early upstroke: wings swept forward at body level, blurred
frames.notes: Head hidden behind the wings. Not measured.

frames.phase: upstroke: wing raised fast, flexed and blurred
frames.notes: Wing a blurred streak; tip read at the end of the blur.

frames.phase: late upstroke: wing extended up and back in an arc
top of stroke: wing near vertical
frames.notes: Wing tip reaches above the frame's main crop (y 1243).

downstrokeShare.computed: tip highest relative to the tail at frames 1, 7, 12; lowest at frame 3 (frame 2 already low) and frame 8 (frame 9, wings forward at body level, not lower). Downstroke 1->3 = 2 intervals of a 6-interval beat; 7->8(-8.5) = 1-1.5 of 5. Half-frame sampling error at each end gives the range.

wingElevationDeg.computed: top = frames 1, 7, 12; bottom = frames 3, 8; frame 2 (mid-downstroke, wing spread sideways) projects at -80.2; upstroke frames 5, 6, 10, 11 range from +75 (wing extended up and back, frames 6, 11) to +128 (flexed and blurred, frame 10). Frames 4 and 9 not measured.

derived.projectedSweepDeg: about 225-230 (from +109..+115 over the back, forward and down to -111..-116 below and ahead of the shoulder)
derived.climb: eye rises about 200 px over 11 intervals relative to the backdrop line (12 px per interval at the start, accelerating)

bodyBob.computed: after a quadratic trend the corrected eye heights leave residuals within +/-6 px (frames 1,2,3,5,6,7,8,10,11,12), about 4% of the eye-to-tail length (about 155 px) and only twice the reading precision; frames 2 and 8 (early/mid downstroke) sit lowest (+4.5, +6.2 px down) and frame 6 highest (-5.9), but the other frames do not follow a clear beat-locked pattern

findings: Wingbeat 8.7 Hz (tops 6 then 5 frames apart at 21 ms; 5.5 frames = 116 ms). The catalogue's 2 cycles agrees here. Same as plate 755 (8.8 Hz) within error: slow, climbing pigeon flight beats at about 8-9 Hz.
Climbing flight again: body 30-38 deg nose up (plate 755: 31-37 deg), eye rising about 18 px per frame on average.

The downstroke is quick: about 30% of the beat (20-45%). The wing goes from near vertical over the back (+109 to +115 deg from the rearward body axis) to below and ahead of the shoulder (-111 to -116 deg) in 1-2 intervals (21-42 ms); in mid-downstroke (frame 2) the wings are spread sideways and the near wing projects below the body. The upstroke takes 3.5-4 intervals: wings swept forward at body level (frames 4, 9, head hidden), then raised flexed (frames 5, 10, blurred) and extended up and back (+75 deg, frames 6, 11) before the next top.
Projected wing length is longest at the top (152-162 px) and shortest when flexed in the upstroke (114-135 px) and in mid-downstroke (95 px, wing pointing toward the camera).

Compared with plate 755 (same pigeon type, 19 ms): same rate, pitch and bottom position (755: -118 to -134); the top here leans a bit further forward (+109..+115 vs +83..+91), and the downstroke share is lower (about 30% vs 42%), both within one frame of sampling. Neither plate supports a downstroke longer than the upstroke for this slow climbing flight.

Compared with figures/goose.json: flap (8 frames at 12 fps, wing rot 0/55/10/60...) beats at 6 Hz and rush at 7 Hz, with the wing swinging +26 to +76 (flap) / +24 to +82 (rush) deg from the rearward body axis and equal up/down time. The pigeon's top (+109..+115) is beyond the goose top, and the goose never takes the wing below or ahead of the body, where the pigeon spends about half of each beat; the pigeon's quick downstroke and slow, flexed upstroke are also absent from the goose. 6-7 Hz is reasonable for a bird bigger than a pigeon (8.7 Hz) and smaller than the vulture (3.8 Hz, plate 765). flap's body rises steadily (y 0 to -9) with no beat-locked bob, which matches this plate.
Not measured: frames 4 and 9 (head hidden by the forward-swept wings); the 12 front views (row 2); the far wing (only its tip in frame 2 is noted); forward speed (each frame is a different camera).
